title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Timber Provision"

Timber provision values the rent the world's forests earn from wood production. The published
figure, `timber_provision_gep`, is the World Bank's Changing Wealth of Nations 2024 forest rent
for 2019, computed here from CWoN's timber revenue and rental rate, one row per country. The
price convention recorded in `es_config.csv` is `stumpage value`.

## The published figure: CWoN forest rent

`gep_calculation` multiplies two tables of the CWoN 2024 reproducibility package
(`FR_WLD_2024_195`, `Output/Latest`): `Forest, timber revenues (current USD)` from
`forest_timber_revenue.xlsx` and `Forest, timber, rental rate` from
`forest_timber_rental_rate.xlsx`, each in its `YR2019` column and matched to the account's
countries on the ISO3 label. This is CWoN's own step, `tot_rent = tot_rev * ratio` in
`forest_timber_depletion.do`. The values are current US dollars of 2019, which is the account's
2019 USD with no further conversion. A country without both inputs stays missing, except the five
countries `forest_timber_gapfill.do` names for a zero rent (San Marino, Monaco, Greenland, the
West Bank and Gaza and Syria), which take zero when their inputs are missing. Syria has both
inputs, so four zeros come from this rule. The total is $132.13bn over 190 positive countries,
with 8 zeros and 52 missing.

The task reads CWoN's published rent, `Forest, rents (current US$)` in
`forest_timber_rent_cd.dta`, only to check the result. The two are equal in all 198 countries
both carry. The published table has 15 further zeros, described under Coverage.

CWoN builds this rent in `forest_timber_depletion.do`. Each product's FAOSTAT production, wood
fuel (item 1864) and industrial roundwood (items 1866 and 1867), is priced at its regional mean
export unit value, after values above the median plus 1.5 times the interquartile range are
replaced by the median. The three revenues are summed, so fuelwood is already inside the figure,
and the sum is multiplied by one rental ratio, country-specific for 17 countries and a regional
default elsewhere. `forest_timber_gapfill.do` then sets the rent to zero where CWoN has no forest
data for small island economies and a few named countries. Its island list,
`general_small_island_economies.csv`, is not in the package, so the account applies the named
countries only.

## Published beside it

- **`timber_provision_gep_spatial`, the comparison construction.** The zonal sum of the Forestry
  pipeline's value raster, $88.74bn over 166 countries (zero elsewhere). It is the construction
  the shared sheet carried before the account adopted the CWoN rent, and it is kept because it is
  the only spatial forestry layer the library holds. It is described under "Spatial comparison
  column" below.
- **`timber_provision_gep_fuelwood_part` and `timber_provision_gep_industrial_part`, an
  approximate split of the published figure** ($59.99bn and $72.14bn, summing to it). Each
  product's FAOSTAT production is priced at its WORLD export unit value, and the fuelwood share of
  that revenue is applied to the CWoN rent. CWoN itself prices with outlier-trimmed regional mean
  export unit values, so this is an approximate allocation, not an exact decomposition of CWoN's
  rent. Its purpose is to show that a separate fuelwood row is a subset of this figure, never an
  addition to it.
- **`timber_roundwood_gross_value`, a diagnostic** ($881.66bn over 202 countries). FAOSTAT
  roundwood production priced at the country's own industrial-roundwood export unit value where
  it falls between $5 and $3,000 per m³, else the world value. A rent above it flags the country
  for review. Export unit values are proxies for the price of the wood actually produced,
  especially where trade is thin, so an exceedance alone does not establish an error in either
  figure.

## Spatial comparison column

### Quantity

Annual harvestable biomass yield in cubic metres per hectare, built from MC2 forest types crossed
with Tian et al. timber regions and adjusted for net primary productivity. This layer is produced
by the consortium drive's Forestry calculation and is staged for the library rather than rebuilt in it.

### Price

The national log price in USD per cubic metre, from Siikamaki and Santiago-Avila 2014 as the
Forestry calculation's method appendix cites it.

### Valuation

Gross return is converted to net return with the GTAP land factor share (Damania et al. 2023) and
then reduced by a per-pixel transport cost built from Weiss et al. travel time and a trucking
cost. `net_forest_return` is that decomposition:

$$
\text{net return} = \text{land factor share} \times \text{biomass} \times \text{price} - \text{transport cost}
$$

`forest_value_from_net_return` keeps a pixel only where the Lesiv et al. (2022) forest management
map marks current timber activity, categories 2 to 5 on forested ESA classes. Negative net returns
and nodata floor to zero, which is the value raster's own nodata convention.

`gep_by_zone` then sums the value raster per country. It runs blockwise with `np.bincount` over
the 10 arcsecond r250 country-id raster, 2048 rows at a time, accumulating into an array indexed by
`iso3_r250_id`. `timber_gep_from_zone_sums` keys those sums onto the country list.

### Checks on the spatial column

The spatial column is the library's own run of the zonal sum over the staged value raster. The
committed Forestry CSV is its anchor, logged next to the computed sum and pinned in the test
suite. Three checks are recorded against the staged rasters:

- `current_forest_value.tif` equals `forestry_land_share_return_tcost_before_2022_07_23.tif`
  bit-exactly on every one of its 265,210,379 positive pixels, with zero mismatches globally. The
  remaining 802,119,863 positive net-return pixels are dropped by the management mask, which is
  external to the staged layers and cannot be derived from them.
- The net-return decomposition reproduces the net-return raster with a per-region fitted land
  factor share, R2 between 0.78 and 0.9999 over twelve continental windows and median relative
  error between 0.5 and 4 percent. The share applies at GTAP region by AEZ level with separate
  plantation and natural estimates, so it enters as an input rather than as a constant.
- The committed per-country table, $88.74bn over 166 countries, is the plain pixel sum of
  `current_forest_value.tif` inside each r250 country polygon, ratio 1.0000 on all countries
  tested. The raster is per-pixel USD.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in constant 2019 USD. Of the 250, 190 carry a value, 8 are zeros and 52 are missing. Four zeros are countries whose FAOSTAT roundwood production is zero (Andorra, the Faroe Islands, Gibraltar and Malta), so their revenue is zero. The other four are the named zeros for Greenland, Monaco, the West Bank and Gaza and San Marino. Of the 52 missing rows, 37 are countries CWoN does not value in 2019, 34 absent from its table plus the Isle of Man, Nauru and Kosovo. The other 15 are small islands and territories with no forest revenue in any year, which CWoN's island rule sets to zero: American Samoa, Antigua and Barbuda, Bermuda, Curaçao, the Cayman Islands, Grenada, Guam, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Martin, the Marshall Islands, the Northern Mariana Islands, Palau, Sint Maarten, Tuvalu and the US Virgin Islands. Without the island list they stay missing. Either way they carry no value, so the total equals CWoN's.

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, scoped to the `timber_provision` service:

- `timber_provision_cwon_forest_revenue_path` and `timber_provision_cwon_forest_rental_rate_path`,
  CWoN's `forest_timber_revenue.xlsx` and `forest_timber_rental_rate.xlsx`, the two factors of
  the rent.
- `timber_provision_cwon_assumed_zero_countries`, the five countries CWoN names for a zero rent.
- `timber_provision_cwon_forest_rent_path`, CWoN's `forest_timber_rent_cd.dta`, the published
  rent the computed one is checked against.
- `timber_provision_faostat_roundwood_path`, the staged FAOSTAT forestry slice for 2019, behind
  the fuelwood split and the gross-value diagnostic.
- `timber_provision_value_raster_path`, the staged current-forest-value raster.
- `timber_provision_zone_raster_path`, `cartographic/ee/ee_r250_id_10sec.tif`, the country-id
  raster the zonal sum keys on.
- `timber_provision_gep_path`, the committed Forestry table, the spatial column's anchor.

## Output

`gep_calculation` writes `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory, holding the
r250 identifiers and attributes, `year`, `timber_provision_gep` (the CWoN rent),
`timber_provision_gep_fuelwood_part`, `timber_provision_gep_industrial_part`,
`timber_provision_gep_spatial` and `timber_roundwood_gross_value`.

## Method constants

`NET_RETURN_NDV = -99999.0` is the net-return raster's nodata value, which
`forest_value_from_net_return` excludes alongside negative returns.

The zonal sum is sized by `n_zones = 1000` and reads `rows_per_block = 2048` at a time.

## Taken as given

CWoN's timber revenue and rental rate are taken as published, and the rent is computed from them.
For the spatial column, the upstream raster valuation
(the biomass yield, the aligned log prices and the transport cost surface) is taken as produced
by the Forestry calculation. The management mask is not derivable from the staged layers and is
likewise adopted.

## What is open

The rent computed from CWoN's revenue and rental rate equals CWoN's published `YR2019` rent in
every country both carry, and the 15 island zeros differ only as missing against zero. It is not
a reproduction of CWoN's revenue or rental ratio, nor of the spatial pipeline, and not a
scientific validation of the rent. A candidate author write-up (`timber_provision_appendix.docx`, last
changed 10 May 2026, in the drive's Forestry folder rather than the methods folder) describes the
spatial model behind `timber_provision_gep_spatial`, not the published rent, and the authors have
been asked to confirm it. Malaysia's CWoN rental ratio is 1.1546 in every year, so its rent
exceeds CWoN's own revenue for it ($6.30bn against $5.46bn). The account takes the ratio as
published until that is decided. The scientific support for CWoN's rental ratio as this service's measure
also remains open.
